symptoms: You may see long papery windows on the leaves of young plants.
The leaves develop ragged holes that get bigger as the pest grows.
Large areas of the leaves may be eaten away completely.
The pest may bore into the corn ears and damage them.
You might see a lot of waste matter left behind by the pests.
favourable_conditions: The pest thrives in tropical and sub-tropical regions where maize is available.
prevention: Plough your field deeply before planting to expose the pests to birds.
Plant your crops at the same time as your neighbors to avoid staggered growth.
Plant rows of pulse crops like pigeon pea or black gram between your maize.
Set up bird perches in the field to attract birds that eat the pests.
Plant trap crops like Napier grass around the edge of your field.
practices: Walk through your field in a W pattern every week to check for damage.
Pick off egg masses and larvae by hand and crush them or drop them in water.
Put a mix of sand and lime or ash into the center of the plant whorl.
Use pheromone traps to catch and destroy the male moths.
Monitor your crop regularly from the time it sprouts.
